A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SafeFix study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison. Reporting inconsistencies affect interpretation but do not prevent matching the material.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on CelebA and ImageNet10, component ablations, attribute-level analyses, and synthetic-data evaluations in Section 5 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 reports original classification and ablation results, plus a human audit, an alternative-generator experiment, and threshold sensitivity results in Section 5 and Appendix G.

M1.justification: The core generation, LVLM filtering, and retraining pipeline is retained. Appendix G.2 adds a variant replacing ControlNet with InstructPix2Pix while retaining Qwen2.5-VL filtering. Section 4.1 also changes the stated rarity check from validation support to training support, aligning it with the training-based definition already present in v1; an implementation change is not established.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CelebA lipstick classification and the same ten ImageNet classes. The human audit, generator substitution, and additional attribute-combination analyses use the existing image domains and tasks rather than introducing new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The main external comparators remain DA-CDM, Mask-ControlNet, HiBug_Class, and HiBug_Task. v2 Table 10 additionally evaluates an InstructPix2Pix-based SafeFix variant against the ControlNet version and those baselines. HiBug2 remains unevaluated.

E3.justification: v2 reports an 8:1:1 train/validation/test split instead of v1's 8:2 train/validation split, including the standalone synthetic-data experiment. It introduces Fix Rate as a headline metric and changes the default accuracy-gap threshold from 0.01 to 0.03. The human audit and threshold sweeps add evaluation procedures. These are reported protocol changes; retained validation wording and Appendix F's old 20,000-image validation set leave implementation consistency unresolved.

E4.justification: v2 adds direct human validation of LVLM filtering and its error types, an InstructPix2Pix substitution test, and explicit rarity/error-threshold sensitivity tables. Section 5.5 also adds findings for larger attribute combinations. These substantially extend the checks on filtering reliability, generator dependence, and diagnosis sensitivity beyond v1's retained ablations and qualitative analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new human audit reports point percentages and average agreement, without introducing an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Main benchmark, component-ablation, attribute-selection, Figure 4, and standalone synthetic-data results are revised. For example, CelebA ResNet with Qwen filtering and 1,000 added images is 91.69% validation accuracy in v1 Table 1 and 91.92% test accuracy in v2 Table 7; these are different-split results, not a same-setting gain. New audit results report background errors falling from 7% to 2% and attribute errors from 24% to 3%. Generator and threshold results are added, while generation-quality scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The substantive slice definitions, rarity/error criteria in Equations (1)–(5), and appendix complexity arguments are retained. No new theorem or proof appears. Equation (6) supplies the adopted Fix Rate formula as part of the evaluation change rather than a new theoretical contribution.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the claims of targeted, semantically faithful, distribution-consistent repair without introducing new bugs. The added human-audit statement supplies supporting evidence for the existing filtering claim rather than redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations about independence from ControlNet, threshold sensitivity, and the disadvantages of larger attribute combinations. It removes Section 5.2's explanation involving synthetic-pattern saturation and diminishing returns, and adds future directions beyond discrete attributes. The main limitations concerning component bias, computation, artifacts, and fixed vocabularies remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents the audit's five AI graduate students and 300 CelebA images, specifies the InstructPix2Pix/Qwen combination, and updates the documented accuracy-gap threshold. Optimizer settings, training duration, hardware, generation prompts, filtering queries, and the code-access link are retained, including details moved out of the main experimental setup.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to InstructPix2Pix and Lai et al.'s model-upgrade work for the Fix Rate metric, and removes OpenFlamingo. The broader positioning relative to HiBug, retrieval-based repair, diffusion augmentation, and LVLM filtering remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The overall section hierarchy and much of the prose are retained. v2 condenses introductory and baseline descriptions, rewrites portions of the results discussion, inserts a human-audit subsection and an accuracy-results appendix, and renames the standalone synthetic-data analysis. These are localized narrative and organizational revisions.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from single-column to two-column layout. Main accuracy tables become Fix Rate displays, with accuracy tables supplied in Appendix E; audit, generator, and threshold tables are added. Figure 4 is redrawn, Figure 3 is substantially reduced in size, and Figures 5–6 rearrange retained examples from horizontal comparisons into stacked panels.

improvement.justification: The human audit and alternative-generator experiment strengthen validation beyond v1, and the stated separate test split could improve evaluation independence. However, v2 retains conflicting split descriptions, changes the error-gap threshold to 0.03 while retaining a diagnosed example with only a 0.0167 gap, and adds Table 13 whose increasing bug counts contradict the stricter criterion in Equation (5). These conflicts affect central repair evidence, preventing a reliable judgment that the benefits outweigh the reporting problems.
